QF.id: AIFM CIII Modern Portfolio Theory and Capital Market Theory_2

question.text: Ms. Priya Shah, Risk Officer at Aravalli Long-Short Fund, is listing the classical assumptions of MPT for her internal model validation memo. Which of the following is NOT a Markowitz-MPT assumption?

answer.text: Investors base decisions solely on expected return and risk.
Investors can borrow and lend unlimited amounts at the risk-free rate.
Given two assets with equal return, investors prefer the one with lower risk.

explanation.text: The Logic: The ability to borrow/lend at the risk-free rate is an assumption of CAPITAL MARKET THEORY (CMT), not of the original Markowitz MPT. MPT assumes (a) return-maximisation for given risk, (b) one-period expected-utility maximisation, (c) decisions on return and risk alone, and (d) risk estimated from variability of expected returns. The Trap: (A), (B) and (D) are literal MPT assumptions listed in Section 3.2 of the chapter. (C) is tempting because it appears in the CMT section 3.11 — but it is NOT in the MPT list. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C and XIX-D test the same MPT-vs-CMT assumption boundary. XXI-B (Portfolio Manager) also tests the risk-free-rate borrowing assumption as a CAPM, not MPT, prerequisite. Manager's Pro-Tip: When regulators (SEBI) ask you to justify your Cat III fund's risk model, always bucket assumptions by MPT (portfolio construction) vs CMT (asset pricing). Your PPM language should not confuse the two — auditors flag this routinely.
